transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, it's getting bad at work. I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and even just basic follow-ups I promised people. It's like my brain just drops the information the second I turn around. And speaking of turning around, the layout of our new supply room is a total disaster. They moved the HVAC filters to the top shelf, and I'm practically climbing the racks to get them. I told Jerry—he's the shift supervisor—that it's a safety hazard, but he just ignores me. He’s been really stressed since his dog had surgery, though. Anyway, the missed work orders have piled up so much that work basically sent me here. They said I need to get this sorted out before I lose my shot at moving up to a senior tech position.
Have you noticed these memory problems happening in other areas of your life, like at home or with personal tasks, or do they seem to only happen at work?

I haven't really noticed it at home, to be honest. I mean, maybe? I'm not sure. I live alone, so it's not like I have a boss tracking my every move there to tell me if I messed up. Well, I do have my dog, Buster. He's a rescue. Actually, speaking of rescues, my truck is basically a rescue at this point. It's an old Chevy and I spend half my weekends just trying to keep it running. 

The alternator went out on me just last week, which was a whole ordeal because the parts store gave me the wrong one. Two different times! You'd think a guy working the counter would know the difference between the mounting brackets, but they just hire kids right out of high school now who don't even know which end of a wrench to hold. It's really frustrating when people don't take pride in their work, you know? I always try to do a good job, which is why my supervisor getting on my case is so... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Did you mean about my house?

Let’s go back to that for a moment—when you said you haven't noticed the memory problems at home, do you mean you haven't forgotten personal appointments, grocery lists, or things you meant to do around the house?

I mean, I don't really make grocery lists in the first place, so there's nothing to forget there. I just sort of go when I'm out of milk or whatever. I usually go to that Food Lion over on 4th street, and honestly, they just rearranged their aisles too, which is a total nightmare. They moved the coffee all the way over to aisle nine next to the pet food. Which makes zero sense to me, who puts coffee next to dog food? 

But I guess it did remind me to get food for Buster. He has been so picky lately, by the way. I bought him this expensive salmon kibble because the vet said his coat looked a little dry, and he just sniffed it and looked at me like I insulted him. Fifty dollars for a bag of food he won't even eat! I ended up having to mix it with wet food and a little bit of warm chicken broth just to get him to touch it. The broth trick usually works, my mom actually taught me that. She used to do that for our golden retriever when I was a kid, back when we lived in Ohio... wait. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What were you asking? Oh, right, appointments and stuff. Um, no, I don't really have a lot of personal appointments to forget, to be honest. It really just feels like it's the work stuff where I'm dropping the ball.

Can you think of any recent situations, even small ones, where you’ve forgotten something important outside of work—like a friend’s birthday, a TV show you meant to watch, or even where you put your keys?

Well, my keys... yeah, actually. Now that you mention it, my keys are a whole situation. But it's not just at home, it's—well, it's mostly at work, honestly. I'm constantly hunting for my keys, or my flashlight, or the work tablet. It's like I'll have a wrench in my hand one second, and the next it's just gone. Poof. And it's getting really bad because it holds up jobs, you know? I'll be in the middle of fixing a leaky pipe in one of the tenant bathrooms, and I have to stop everything to look for the pipe sealant I just set down. 

The tenants get so annoyed. This one lady in 4B, she was already mad because her cat got out into the hallway—which wasn't my fault, she left the door propped open with a shoe—but she stood there tapping her foot while I tore my toolbag apart looking for my pliers. Her cat was this huge orange tabby, kind of looked like Garfield but meaner. It hissed at me when I tried to pet it. I don't really get cats. Dogs are so much better, they actually want to be around you. Buster is always right at my heels when I'm home. But anyway, yeah, I lose my tools and stuff constantly. It makes me look so careless, and Jerry's definitely noticed. He made this passive-aggressive comment the other day about attaching a tracking device to my toolbelt. Which, honestly, might not be a terrible idea if they made them small enough. Do they make those for tools? I know they have them for wallets now... wait, what was the question? Keys? Yeah, I lose those all the time.
Have you ever had any head injuries or trauma, like a concussion or something more serious, that might be affecting your memory?

Head injuries? No, I don't think so. I mean, I've bumped my head on pipes and stuff crawling around under sinks, but nothing major. Never had a concussion or anything that knocked me out. Though, I did fall off a ladder once when I was about twenty. I was helping my uncle paint his barn out in the country. It was this really bright, barn-red color, you know the classic kind? We had to mix the paint ourselves in these huge buckets. 

Anyway, the ladder wasn't set right in the dirt, and I just tumbled backward into a rosebush. Scratched up my arms pretty bad, and I ruined my favorite pair of overalls. They were those real sturdy Carhartt ones, too. They don't make them like they used to, honestly. The denim they use now feels so thin, it rips if you just look at it wrong. I bought a new pair last month for work, and the knee is already wearing thin from just kneeling on the tile in the bathrooms. I should probably get those knee pads, but they're always so bulky and they slide down your leg when you walk. Jerry wears them, but he waddles around like a penguin when he has them on. It's kind of funny to watch, actually. But um... no, my head is fine. No injuries there.
Lately, have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Down? No, not really. I mean, I'm stressed about work and Jerry and all that, but I wouldn't say I'm hopeless or anything. I still like doing my usual stuff. Well, when I actually have the time and energy for it, anyway. Like, I love working in my garden. I have these tomato plants that are just going crazy this year. I tried this new fertilizer, it's like a fish emulsion thing? It smells absolutely terrible, like low tide on a hot day, but the plants love it. 

My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she actually complained about the smell. She's always complaining about something, though. Last week it was because my recycling bin was out on the curb for an extra day. She left this typed note taped to the lid. Who types a note for that? She must have this old typewriter in her house, because the font looked like it was from the 1970s. It made me think of my grandmother's house, she had this heavy green typewriter on her desk that I used to play with when I was little. The keys were so hard to press down, you really had to jam your fingers into them. I used to pretend I was a reporter for a big newspaper... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, feeling down. No, I'm not depressed or anything like that. Just frustrated with the work situation.
Have you been feeling unusually worried, anxious, or on edge lately, especially when you're trying to focus or remember things?

Anxious? No, I wouldn't say I'm anxious. I mean, I get frustrated, like I said, especially when I can't find my tools and Jerry's breathing down my neck. But not like, worried or on edge in a bad way. Just annoyed. It's like when you're trying to untangle a really bad knot in an extension cord, you know? We have these bright orange ones at work, and I swear the other guys just throw them in the back of the van in a giant pile. 

I spent an hour last Tuesday just trying to get one free so I could run a power drill out to the courtyard. The fountain out there was acting up—the pump filter was completely clogged with these little oak leaves. The oak tree out there is massive, it drops leaves year-round. It makes a huge mess. The groundskeeper, Hector, he's always out there with his leaf blower, but it's like a losing battle. He has this really nice electric one, though. It's so much quieter than the gas ones. My neighbor across the street has a gas one, and he fires it up at 7 AM on Saturdays. It drives Buster absolutely crazy, he barks at the window until I have to close the blinds. But yeah, no, I don't feel worried or anxious. Just normal work stress, really.
Outside of work, do you rely on reminders like phone alerts, notes, or calendars to help you remember things you need to do around the house or with friends?

Reminders? Oh, yeah. I mean, I have to, right? If I don't write it down, it's just gone. But honestly, even with notes, it's a mess. Actually, that's kind of the whole reason I'm here. I keep forgetting to make these scheduled callbacks to clients, and I'm losing track of work orders... even just basic follow-ups I promised people. It's gotten so bad, it's all piled up, and work basically told me I needed to come see someone before I blow my chance at getting promoted. 

Which is frustrating because I've been there forever. And I try with the notes! I have these little yellow sticky notes everywhere. I put them on the dashboard of my truck, but then the defroster blows them off, and they end up under the seat with the old fast-food wrappers. I found one from like, three months ago when I was cleaning out the truck last weekend. It just said "Call Dave about the pipe," and I stood there for ten minutes trying to figure out which Dave and which pipe. I know three Daves! There's Dave from the hardware store, Dave my cousin who always wants to borrow my power washer, and Dave from the second floor of the apartment complex we manage. 

The apartment Dave is a real piece of work, by the way. He has this tiny little yappy dog that he lets run around without a leash, even though it's strictly against the lease agreement. I've told him a hundred times, but he just smiles and says "Oh, Princess wouldn't hurt a fly." Meanwhile, Princess is trying to bite my ankles while I'm trying to fix his garbage disposal. Garbage disposals are the worst, people put everything down there. I pulled a whole chicken bone out of one last week. How do you even do that by accident? But yeah, the forgetting things... it's a real problem at work right now. They're pretty fed up with me dropping the ball on the callbacks and orders.
When you're at home or out with friends, do you find yourself forgetting things even when you've set reminders or written them down?

Well, at home it's... I mean, I guess I do forget stuff, like grabbing milk or calling my sister back. But honestly, that's not even the main issue. It's work. Like I was saying, that's exactly what brought me in here. I keep forgetting those scheduled callbacks and work orders. And just basic follow-ups I promised people! I'll tell a tenant, "Hey, I'll be back in ten minutes with a new washer for that faucet," and then my boss, Jerry, flags me down about a broken railing, and poof, the faucet is completely gone from my brain. 

Speaking of Jerry, he's got this new truck, right? A brand-new Ford F-150, cherry red. It's beautiful, but he's so paranoid about getting a scratch on it that he parks it taking up two spots in the far corner of the lot. Which is ridiculous because the lot is tiny anyway, and half the time the garbage truck can't even get in to empty the dumpsters. The garbage guys get so mad. They honk this incredibly loud horn. It sounds like a freight train right outside the office window. It startles me every single time, makes me spill my coffee. I drink way too much coffee, probably. I get those big tubs from the warehouse store, the hazelnut kind. My sister says hazelnut coffee smells like burning plastic, but I love it. We argue about it every time she comes over. She only drinks tea. Peppermint tea, specifically. 

But anyway, yeah, the forgetting at work... it's piled up so much. All those missed calls and lost work orders. It got to the point where work basically sent me here. They told me I needed to get this sorted out before I lose my shot at moving up to a supervisor role. Which I really want, you know? I've put in my time. I just... the stuff just slips right out of my head.
Do you drink alcohol, and if so, how often or how much would you say you typically consume in a week?

Alcohol? No, I don't really drink. Never really got a taste for it, honestly. Maybe a beer at a barbecue once in a blue moon, but that's about it. Last time I had one was... gosh, probably my cousin's Fourth of July party. He always gets those fancy craft beers, you know? The ones with the crazy labels. He had one that was supposed to taste like grapefruit and pine needles, which sounds awful, right? But he swore by it. He actually brews his own stuff in his garage now. It smells terrible when he's doing it, like old bread and yeast. His wife hates it. She makes him keep the garage door open, but then all the flies get in. 

And they live near this dairy farm, so the flies are just relentless. Huge, fat ones. You can't even sit on their patio without swatting them away constantly. They bought one of those bug zappers, the blue light ones? It's so loud. Every time a bug hits it, it makes this loud *zap* sound, like a tiny firecracker. It drives my dog Buster crazy, he tries to hide under the picnic table. Buster hates loud noises. Thunderstorms, fireworks, bug zappers... he's a nervous wreck. But yeah, no, I don't really drink alcohol. Just my hazelnut coffee, mostly.

Well, at home it's... I mean, I guess I do forget stuff, like grabbing milk or calling my sister back. But honestly, that's not even the main issue. It's work. Like I was saying, that's exactly what brought me in here. I keep forgetting those scheduled callbacks and work orders. And just basic follow-ups I promised people! I'll tell a tenant, "Hey, I'll be back in ten minutes with a new washer for that faucet," and then my boss, Jerry, flags me down about a broken railing, and poof, the faucet is completely gone from my brain. 

Speaking of Jerry, he's got this new truck, right? A brand-new Ford F-150, cherry red. It's beautiful, but he's so paranoid about getting a scratch on it that he parks it taking up two spots in the far corner of the lot. Which is ridiculous because the lot is tiny anyway, and half the time the garbage truck can't even get in to empty the dumpsters. The garbage guys get so mad. They honk this incredibly loud horn. It sounds like a freight train right outside the office window. It startles me every single time, makes me spill my coffee. I drink way too much coffee, probably. I get those big tubs from the warehouse store, the hazelnut kind. My sister says hazelnut coffee smells like burning plastic, but I love it. We argue about it every time she comes over. She only drinks tea. Peppermint tea, specifically. 

But anyway, yeah, the forgetting at work... it's piled up so much. All those missed calls and lost work orders. It got to the point where work basically sent me here. They told me I needed to get this sorted out before I lose my shot at moving up to a supervisor role. Which I really want, you know? I've put in my time. I just... the stuff just slips right out of my head.

doctor.intent: Determine if there is a history of alcohol use or abuse, which would support a diagnosis of F10.10 (Alcohol Use Disorder, Mild).
doctor.question: Do you drink alcohol, and if so, how often or how much would you say you typically consume in a week?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about alcohol consumption, which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Alcohol? No, I don't really drink. Never really got a taste for it, honestly. Maybe a beer at a barbecue once in a blue moon, but that's about it. Last time I had one was... gosh, probably my cousin's Fourth of July party. He always gets those fancy craft beers, you know? The ones with the crazy labels. He had one that was supposed to taste like grapefruit and pine needles, which sounds awful, right? But he swore by it. He actually brews his own stuff in his garage now. It smells terrible when he's doing it, like old bread and yeast. His wife hates it. She makes him keep the garage door open, but then all the flies get in. 

And they live near this dairy farm, so the flies are just relentless. Huge, fat ones. You can't even sit on their patio without swatting them away constantly. They bought one of those bug zappers, the blue light ones? It's so loud. Every time a bug hits it, it makes this loud *zap* sound, like a tiny firecracker. It drives my dog Buster crazy, he tries to hide under the picnic table. Buster hates loud noises. Thunderstorms, fireworks, bug zappers... he's a nervous wreck. But yeah, no, I don't really drink alcohol. Just my hazelnut coffee, mostly.
